title: Fractions and decimals on a number line
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:21Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, Converting fractions, decimals and percentages, is mainly about conversions and percentages and only touches the number line in one bullet, so no bank point teaches placing and comparing fractions, decimals and mixed numbers on a number line.

draft.title: Fractions and decimals on a number line
card: A number line places numbers in order. Numbers to the right are greater. Numbers to the left are less. Negative numbers sit to the left of 0.
To place a fraction, split each gap between whole numbers into equal parts. The denominator tells you how many parts. For \(\frac{3}{4}\), split the gap from 0 to 1 into 4 parts and count 3.
A mixed number sits between two whole numbers. \(2\frac{1}{2}\) is halfway between 2 and 3. A negative mixed number such as \(-2\frac{1}{2}\) is halfway between \(-3\) and \(-2\).
To compare a fraction and a decimal, write both in the same form. For example, \(\frac{3}{4} = 0.75\), so \(\frac{3}{4}\) is greater than \(0.7\). Among negatives, the number closer to 0 is greater.

2.alt: A number line from 0 to 1 with points at 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, which are one quarter, one half and three quarters.

draft.remember: Write numbers in the same form to compare them. The number further right is greater.

a.q: Which number is halfway between \(-3\) and \(-2\) on a number line?
a.why: Halfway between \(-3\) and \(-2\) is \(-2.5\), which is \(-2\frac{1}{2}\). The tempting \(-3\frac{1}{2}\) is halfway between \(-4\) and \(-3\), so it is further left.
a.clue: Think of the gap between \(-3\) and \(-2\), and split it in two.

b.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
b.why: In decimals the numbers are \(-0.8, -0.5, 0.6, 0.75\), which is least to greatest. The second list is wrong because \(-0.8\) is further left than \(-\frac{1}{2}\), so it is less.
b.clue: Change every number to a decimal first.
